==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/bɔː/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/boɹ/|a=GenAm}}
* {{IPA|en|/bo(ː)ɹ/|a=rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{IPA|en|/boə/|a=non-rhotic,non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-bore.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|boar|Bohr|;|boor<aa:pour-poor>}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=pierce|:inh|enm:boren<ety:inh<ang:borian>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|boren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|borian|t=to pierce}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*borōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*burōną}}.

Compare {{cog|da|bore}}, {{cog|nb|bore}}, {{cog|nl|boren}}, {{cog|de|bohren}}, {{cog|non|bora}}. Cognate with {{cog|la|forō||to bore, to pierce}}, {{cog|la|feriō||strike, cut}} and {{cog|sq|birë||hole}}. Sense of wearying may come from a figurative use such as "to bore the ears"; compare German {{m|de|drillen}}.

[[File:Auger (PSF).png|thumb|'''Boring''' a hole through a wooden plank with an [[auger]].]]

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|to inspire boredom}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[inspire]] [[boredom]] in somebody.
#: {{ant|en|interest}}
#: {{co|en|to '''bore''' someone [[to death]]}}
#: {{ux|en|Reading books really '''bores''' me; films are much more exciting.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|I|i|page=206|passage=He '''bores''' me with some trick.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1881|author=w:Thomas Carlyle|title=Reminiscences
|passage={{...}} used to come and '''bore''' me at rare intervals.}}
# {{senseid|en|to make a hole}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To make a [[hole]] through something.
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:make a hole}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|III|ii|passage=I'll believe as soon this whole earth may be '''bored'''.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make a [[hole]] with, or as if with, a boring instrument; to cut a circular hole by the rotary motion of a tool.
#: {{co|en|to '''bore''' for water or oil}}
#: {{ux|en|An insect '''bores''' into a tree.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1911|author={{w|Steele Rudd|‘Steel Rudd’}}|title=The Book of Dan|location=Brisbane|publisher=University of Queensland Press|year_published=1970|page=1|passage=‘You give me twelve bob a foot, an’ I’ll bloomin’ quick show you whether I can '''bore''' or not.’}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To form or enlarge (something) by means of a boring instrument or apparatus.
#: {{co|en|to '''bore''' a steam cylinder or a gun barrel; to '''bore''' a hole}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1862|author=w:Thaddeus William Harris|title=A Treatise on Some of the Insects Injurious to Vegetation
|passage=short but very powerful jaws, by means whereof the insect can '''bore''' {{...}} a cylindrical passage through the most solid wood}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make (a passage) by laborious effort, as in boring; to force a narrow and difficult passage through.
#: {{co|en|to '''bore''' one’s way through a crowd}}
#* {{RQ:John Gay Trivia|page=79|passage=What bustling crowds I '''bored'''.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be pierced or penetrated by an instrument that cuts as it turns.
#: {{ux|en|This timber does not '''bore''' well.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[glare]] (as if to drill a hole with the eyes).
#: {{ux|en|Their eyes '''bore''' into my back.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|sports|slang}} To [[push]] or [[drive]] (a boxer into the ropes, a boat out of its course, etc.).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1824|author=Pierce Egan|title=Boxiana; Or, Sketches of Ancient and Modern Pugilism|page=600
|passage=The right hand of Curtis was open too much ; but he nevertheless had the best of the hitting in this round, till Inglis '''bored''' him down, out of the ropes.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1885|author=Tresham Gilbey|journal=Baily's Magazine of Sports and Pastimes|volume=43|page=107
|passage=Hanlan, it seems, led at about a mile, when Beach's steamer '''bored''' him, and to avoid the danger of being swamped, he put on a violent spurt and drew well clear of Beach, getting some lengths lead.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To push forward in a certain direction with laborious effort.
#* {{RQ:Dryden Georgics|3|passage=They take their flight {{...}} '''boring''' to the west.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[fool]]; to [[trick]].
# {{lb|en|MLE|slang}} To inflict a [[wound]] upon by means of a [[knife]], to [[stab]].
#: {{syn|en|chef up|juke|jook|ching|ying|shank|splash|juice up}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|hole cut into something}} A [[hole]] [[drill]]ed, [[bore#Verb|bore]]d{{,}} or [[mill#Verb|mill]]ed through something.
#: {{coi|en|the '''bore''' of a cannon}}
#* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|edition=3rd|century=II|page=53|passage=the '''bores''' of wind-instruments}}
# {{lb|en|AU}} A [[borehole]] sunk into an [[artesian]] [[basin]] to provide a source of water.
#: {{synonyms|en|artesian bore|artesian well}}
# {{senseid|en|hole diameter}} The [[diameter]] of such a hole.
## {{senseid|en|Q245657}} {{lb|en|especially}} The [[diameter]] of a [[cylinder]] in a [[piston engine]] or [[compressor]].
##: {{cot|en|stroke<id:Q56296612>}}
##: {{ux|en|The '''bore''' times the stroke times the number of cylinders equals displacement.}}
# The tunnel inside of a gun's [[barrel]] through which the bullet travels when fired, or (by extension) its [[diameter]].
# A tool, such as an [[auger]], for making a hole by boring.
# A [[cap]]ped well drilled to tap [[artesian]] [[water]].
## The place where such a well exists.
# {{senseid|en|one who inspires boredom}} One who inspires [[boredom]] or [[lack]] of [[interest]]; an uninteresting person.
#: {{ux|en|My neighbour is such a '''bore''' when he talks about his coin collection.}}
# Something [[dull]] or [[uninteresting]].
#: {{ux|en|What a '''bore''' that movie was! There was no action, and the dialogue was totally uncreative.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|author=w:Nathaniel Hawthorne|title=Passages from the French and Italian Notebooks
|passage=It is as great a '''bore''' as to hear a poet read his own verses.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CSL|volume=1|page=2|text=For having submitted my ears to Acutilius for several days (and I think you know his style), I should scarcely have regarded it as a hardship to write you a letter describing his grumblings after patiently enduring the '''bore''' (and it ''was'' rather a '''bore''', I can tell you) of hearing them.}}
# [[calibre|Calibre]]; [[importance]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|IV|vi|passage=Yet are they much too light for the '''bore''' of the matter.}}

===Etymology 2===
